main_text.p: tilia pondera ventris commodè excernantur, uti de Bile loquitur Galenus lib. v. de usu part. cap. 3. Nec hoc tantum, sed & affluentes illi humores incidunt pituitam viscidam, qua intestinorum parietes si non purgarentur nimium confpurcarentur & incruftarentur, utpote quæ etiam naturaliter difpofita funt loca τελμαπώδεα, paludosa, cænosa, putredinibus apta, uti loquitur Galenus lib. de gland. ad Hipp. quâ pituitâ fenfus intestinorum nimium obtunderetur, atque venarum lactearum pori, aliiqué per quos segregatus chylus ad reliquum corpus affluit, occluderentur & obstruerentur, qualem fere usum, quia Galeni tempore pancreas, hoc demum seculo à Wirzungio inventum, nondum innotuerat, soli quoque bili adscripsit, quod utrique humori, videlicet bili & succo pancreatico competit; postquam enim demonstrasset pituitæ copiam in intestino gigni, niniam

page.notes: Greek word in italics as printed: "τελμαπώδεα" is a reconstruction from a small, poorly legible print; treat as doubtful. Word "niniam" at the line end reads "nimiam" (the final line is a catchword-like continuation, printed as "miam" after a hyphen); transcribed as printed with doubt. Some words in the scan (e.g. "viscidam", "confpurcarentur") are set with long s rendered as s.
